chunks.text: 31-year-old female, Unemployed, resident of Bishan, Singapore.
General anesthesia with LMA, propofol induction, remifentanil infusion, and vecuronium for muscle relaxation; desflurane maintenance
General anesthesia for laparoscopic appendectomy at age 24; no adverse events

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Lim from the anesthesia team. Today, we'll go over some questions to prepare you for your laparoscopic gallbladder surgery. Let's start with your medical history. Can you tell me about your gallstones?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, yes. Been having belly pains on the right side, especially after eating. Ultrasound showed stones, so doctor said remove it laparoscopically.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Let's move to your medications. You're on atorvastatin, metformin, and omeprazole daily. What about simvastatin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, I stopped that one already, doc. Was taking it at night, but surgeon said to stop before surgery, right?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Correct. Now, about allergies. Your records say 'no allergies recorded,' but I like to double-check. Have you ever had reactions to antibiotics, especially penicillin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Actually, yes! When I took penicillin for a throat infection years ago, I got a bad rash all over. But it wasn't written down, I guess.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. We'll update your records immediately. Any other allergies or reactions?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, just that one. Never had problems with other antibiotics.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Let's discuss your health conditions. You have hypertension and hyperlipidemia. How are they managed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Blood pressure is okay with the meds, doc. Cholesterol too. But my weight... BMI 28, still struggling with that.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Noted. Have you fasted since midnight as instructed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, nothing since last night's dinner. Just water this morning for meds.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Any previous surgeries or anesthesia issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Appendectomy when I was young. No problems then. Woke up fine.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Lastly, can you walk up stairs without difficulty?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yeah, can climb stairs no problem. Just slower because of the weight, lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll use general anesthesia with a laryngeal mask, propofol, remifentanil, and vecuronium as planned. Desflurane will maintain your anesthesia. Any questions?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doc. Just want to get this done and feel better.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] LMA placed, size four, good seal

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:03] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty-five, atropine one milligram given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:04] remifentanil infusion started at zero point five mcg/kg/min

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] 18-gauge IV access established, blood loss minimal

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:06] vecuronium thirty milligrams given for muscle relaxation

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] crystalloid bolus one thousand mL given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] heart rate increased to one twenty, labetalol ten milligrams IV administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I’m okay, Doctor. A bit tired, but manageable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe a 4? It’s a dull ache where they made the cuts.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or vomiting since waking up? Sometimes the anesthesia can cause that.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A little queasy, but not throwing up. I didn’t eat anything yet anyway.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Are you having any trouble breathing or feeling short of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, breathing’s fine. Just a bit of sore throat from the tube, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything from the operating room, or was everything fuzzy?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don’t remember anything. One minute I was talking, next I was waking up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Given your blood pressure and weight, any chest pain or unusual symptoms?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No chest pain. My BP’s been okay, right? I’ve been taking my meds regularly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: All looks stable. We’ll keep monitoring, but you’re doing well. Rest now, and we’ll get you mobilizing soon.

31-year-old female post-elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Intra-operative management included propofol induction, remifentanil infusion, vecuronium for paralysis, and desflurane via LMA. Notable events: MAP dropped to 55 mmHg (treated with atropine), HR spiked to 120 bpm (treated with labetalol), minimal blood loss.

History of hypertension (medication-managed), obesity (BMI 28), and prior laparoscopic appendectomy at 24 (no prior anesthesia issues). Medications: atorvastatin 20mg daily, metformin 500mg BID, omeprazole 20mg daily. Stopped simvastatin pre-op. Penicillin allergy (rash). Fasting since midnight. ASA II.

Airway watch indicated due to obesity and LMA use. Hemodynamic instability risk from hypertension and intra-op BP fluctuations (MAP 55 mmHg, HR 120 bpm). Glycemic monitoring needed for metformin user. High PONV risk (laparoscopic surgery, opioids, obesity, female gender). Analgesia needs expected post-cholecystectomy. Neuromuscular blockade monitoring required (vecuronium without reversal). Penicillin allergy precautions.

Monitor airway/oxygenation closely. Continue BP/HR vigilance; consider antihypertensives PRN. Check blood glucose regularly. Administer PONV prophylaxis. Provide multimodal analgesia. Assess for residual paralysis (e.g., TOF monitor). Avoid penicillin/cephalosporins.
